providers.title: Providers
providers.lead: A provider is an endpoint that serves models. The key stays encrypted on your machine and never reaches this window.
providers.empty: No providers yet. Search for one below, or use a compatible endpoint.
providers.name: Name
providers.baseUrlHint: Only for compatible endpoints: OpenRouter, a corporate gateway, a model on your own machine.
providers.apiKeyHint: Encrypted with the operating system keyring. Nothing can read it back from here.
providers.foundInEnv: I found a key in `{{name}}`. Use it?
providers.failed: The provider could not be saved.
providers.keyringUnavailable: The operating system keyring cannot be reached, so the key cannot be stored safely. The provider was not saved.
providers.gone: This provider is gone: it may have been deleted elsewhere.
providers.unserved: babelBook does not serve this provider: add it as a compatible endpoint, giving its address.
providers.compatibleHint: The way to what the catalogue does not know: a corporate gateway, a model you serve yourself. The model list comes from the endpoint.
providers.noKeyNeeded: No key needed: it runs on your machine.
providers.findFailed: The model list could not be asked for.
providers.catalogRefreshFailed: No update: the catalogue stays as it was.
providers.catalogBadImport: The file is not a catalogue: nothing was installed.

popular.anthropic: The Claude models, straight from their maker.
popular.openai: The GPT models, straight from their maker.
popular.google: The Gemini models, straight from their maker.
popular.openrouter: One account, hundreds of models from different providers.
popular.mistral: European models, with good results on the Romance languages.
popular.groq: Very fast responses on open models.
popular.xai: The Grok models, straight from their maker.
popular.deepseek: Inexpensive models with good results on long texts.
popular.togetherai: Many open models on a single endpoint.
popular.cerebras: Open models served with very low latency.

glossaries.title: Glossaries
glossaries.lead: A glossary applies to every book that uses it. Changing its terms invalidates translations made under the previous version.
glossaries.empty: No glossaries. Create one, or import one written elsewhere.
glossaries.name: Name
glossaries.descriptionHint: The domain vote reads it to decide whether this glossary applies to a book.
glossaries.versionHint: Saving with changed terms raises the version, and that is what makes books using this glossary translate again.
glossaries.failed: The glossary could not be saved.

prefs.concurrencyHint: How many requests to the model at once. Higher is faster and costs the same, but some providers rate-limit.
prefs.epubcheckHint: Optional, and it needs Java. Without it the report says the check did not run, rather than calling it a pass.
prefs.failed: The setting could not be saved.

quit.confirm: A translation is in flight. Quitting pauses it: when the app reopens it can resume without retranslating what is already done.

deleteProject.message: Delete “{{title}}”? The project, its workspace and the translated EPUB will be removed.

abandonProject.message: Abandon creating “{{title}}”? The project just analysed and its workspace will be removed.

deleteProvider.message: Disconnect “{{name}}”? Its encrypted key will be removed too.

reasoningChange.message: Change reasoning for “{{model}}” on “{{name}}”? Translations already made with this model were cached under the previous setting and will be done again.

contractChange.message: Change the model or a language of “{{title}}”? The {{done}} units already translated were tied to the previous configuration: they stay on disk, but they will stop counting.

deleteGlossary.message: Delete the glossary “{{name}}”? {{count}} projects will lose its terminology.
deleteGlossary.messageOne: Delete the glossary “{{name}}”? One project will lose its terminology.
deleteGlossary.messageNone: Delete the glossary “{{name}}”? No project uses it.
